description: Extraterrestrial base-site targets scored against the Earth predictor stack. Every criterion carries its own dataset_id and source_url. A criterion is given either as a measured 'value' in the Earth predictor's units, or - where the measurement was made at a scale the 0.5 degree Earth grid cannot resolve - as an 'earth_percentile' terrain class, with the original measurement kept in 'measured_value' and explained in 'definition_note'. A criterion whose 'value' is null is not used for that target (weight forced to 0). A target may set its own default 'weights' and a 'validation_tag' selecting which known-analog sites count as positives.
units_note: Targets are compared with Earth through proxies, not identities. Values beyond anything found on Earth are scored against Earth's most extreme value (0.5th/99.5th percentile over land), and terrain criteria measured at metre scales are expressed as Earth-percentile terrain classes. Treat the ranking as a screening tool, not a site survey.

targets.name: Lunar South Pole (Shackleton rim)
targets.source_label: Gawronska et al. (2022), Planet. Sci. J., geologic context and EVA targets at the lunar south pole
targets.summary: Artemis III candidate region on the rim of Shackleton crater: permanently shadowed volatile cold traps next to high-illumination ridges, over extremely rugged polar topography.

precipitation.definition_note: The Moon has no atmosphere and therefore no precipitation. Scored against Earth's driest land.

vegetation.definition_note: No biosphere: the surface is bare regolith. The Earth equivalent is ground with no detectable vegetation (NDVI near 0).

annual_temperature_range.definition_note: Lower bound: seasonally shadowed regions poleward of 80 deg S show >=100 K variation in maximum surface temperature between summer and winter (LRO Diviner polar maps). This is beyond anything on Earth, so it is scored against Earth's largest annual range.

lst_diurnal_range.definition_note: Noon-to-midnight variation of bolometric brightness temperature at 85 degrees latitude from LRO Diviner (about 290 K at the equator). No Earth surface swings this much, so it is scored against Earth's largest day-night swing.

slope.definition_note: Measured: mean slope 9.5 deg over all terrain poleward of 80 S (Chang'E-2 20 m DEM). A 20 m slope cannot be compared with a ~55 km regional slope, so the target is the terrain class 'rugged': Earth's 85th-percentile regional slope. Replace with a matched-scale value once PGDA Product 78 slope maps are processed.

roughness.definition_note: Measured: ~1 m RMS height about a local plane at a 5-10 m baseline (LOLA, Shackleton exterior, walls, floor and rim). The Earth predictor uses a ~28 km window, so the target is the terrain class 'rugged' (km-scale crater and massif relief): Earth's 85th-percentile roughness.

elevation.definition_note: Elevation on the Shackleton rim from a LOLA 5 m/pixel DEM, relative to the mean lunar radius. Not comparable with Earth's sea-level datum; weighted 0 by default.

mean_annual_temperature.definition_note: Not used for this target: the site is sunlit or seasonally lit, so absolute temperature is not the engineering challenge being matched.

basaltic_volcanic.definition_note: Not used: rock type is not part of this site's signature. Only the lava-tube habitat target scores basaltic rock.

targets.name: Malapert Massif, Moon
targets.location_note: Pin shows Malapert crater (84.9 S, 12.9 E). The massif is the ~5 km-high rise formed partly by the crater's south-western rim, with its peak close to 0 deg longitude.
targets.source_label: NASA (28 Oct 2024): Malapert Massif is one of nine Artemis III candidate landing regions
targets.summary: Artemis III candidate landing region on a ~5 km-high massif near the south pole, in sight of both Earth and Shackleton crater: high, sunlit and very rugged terrain.

precipitation.definition_note: The Moon has no atmosphere and therefore no precipitation. Scored against Earth's driest land.

vegetation.definition_note: No biosphere: the surface is bare regolith. The Earth equivalent is ground with no detectable vegetation (NDVI near 0).

annual_temperature_range.definition_note: Lower bound: seasonally shadowed regions poleward of 80 deg S show >=100 K variation in maximum surface temperature between summer and winter (LRO Diviner polar maps). This is beyond anything on Earth, so it is scored against Earth's largest annual range.

lst_diurnal_range.definition_note: Noon-to-midnight variation of bolometric brightness temperature at 85 degrees latitude from LRO Diviner (about 290 K at the equator). No Earth surface swings this much, so it is scored against Earth's largest day-night swing.

slope.baseline: regional mean of the polar region, 20 m posts
slope.definition_note: A ~5 km-high rise (Malapert Mountain) is steeper than the average polar terrain (9.5 deg mean slope poleward of 80 S, Chang'E-2 20 m DEM), so the terrain class is 'very rugged': Earth's 95th-percentile regional slope. Editorial class, not a measurement; replace with PGDA Product 78 slopes.

roughness.definition_note: Kilometre-scale relief of a 5 km massif puts it in the 'very rugged' class: Earth's 95th-percentile roughness. Editorial class, not a measurement.

elevation.definition_note: Not used: lunar heights are measured from the Moon's own datum.

mean_annual_temperature.definition_note: Not used for this target: the site is sunlit or seasonally lit, so absolute temperature is not the engineering challenge being matched.

basaltic_volcanic.definition_note: Not used: rock type is not part of this site's signature. Only the lava-tube habitat target scores basaltic rock.

targets.name: Haworth crater cold trap, Moon
targets.source_label: NASA (28 Oct 2024): Haworth is one of nine Artemis III candidate landing regions
targets.summary: Permanently shadowed crater near the south pole, among the coldest places on the Moon: a cold trap for water ice. Earth cannot reach its temperature, so the match is to Earth's coldest, driest, most thermally stable land.

precipitation.definition_note: The Moon has no atmosphere and therefore no precipitation. Scored against Earth's driest land.

vegetation.definition_note: No biosphere: the surface is bare regolith. The Earth equivalent is ground with no detectable vegetation (NDVI near 0).

mean_annual_temperature.definition_note: Many of Haworth's permanently shadowed regions are believed never to exceed 40 K (-233 C). Far colder than anywhere on Earth, so it is matched to Earth's coldest land. Weighted x2 for this target because 'cold' is the defining challenge of a cold trap.

annual_temperature_range.definition_note: Shadowed regions that never exceed 40 K cannot swing much between seasons, so the class is 'very stable': Earth's 5th-percentile annual range. Editorial class; the measured_value is the 40 K ceiling, not a range.

lst_diurnal_range.definition_note: Permanently shadowed ground never receives direct sunlight, so there is no solar day-night swing; matched to Earth's smallest swing.

slope.definition_note: Not used: terrain inside the shadowed floor is not characterised here. Add it from PGDA Product 78 (Haworth files).

elevation.definition_note: Not used: lunar heights are measured from the Moon's own datum.

basaltic_volcanic.definition_note: Not used: rock type is not part of this site's signature. Only the lava-tube habitat target scores basaltic rock.

targets.name: Marius Hills Pit lava-tube skylight, Moon
targets.source_label: LROC Lunar Pit Atlas: Marius Hills Pit, 14.09°N 303.23°E, 40 m deep, mare terrain
targets.summary: A collapse pit in the Marius Hills that opens into a lava tube: a natural shelter from radiation, micrometeoroids and the surface temperature extremes. Deep lunar lava tubes stay at about 17 °C, so the Earth match is basaltic lava-tube country in a mild, stable climate.
targets.location_note: Matched by its interior: the habitat is inside the tube, so the surface day-night swing is not used. Rock type comes from the Global Lithological Map (GLiM).

precipitation.definition_note: The Moon has no atmosphere and therefore no precipitation. Scored against Earth's driest land.

vegetation.definition_note: No biosphere: the surface is bare regolith. The Earth equivalent is ground with no detectable vegetation (NDVI near 0).

annual_temperature_range.definition_note: Deep lunar lava tubes keep 'a stable temperature of 17 °C (63 °F)', so the seasonal swing inside is taken as close to zero and matched to Earth's smallest annual range. An editorial reading of 'stable'.

lst_diurnal_range.definition_note: Not used: the habitat is inside the tube, which is insulated from the surface day-night swing, so the surface swing does not describe it.

slope.definition_note: The pit lies on mare terrain, which is gentle at regional scale. Estimated class: Earth's 30th-percentile regional slope. No slope was measured at a comparable scale.

roughness.definition_note: Not used: no roughness measured at a scale comparable with Earth's 55 km cells.

elevation.definition_note: Not used: lunar heights are measured from the Moon's own datum.

mean_annual_temperature.definition_note: Deep lunar lava tubes, under 40 m or more of basalt, keep 'a stable temperature of 17 °C (63 °F)'. Matched to Earth's mean annual air temperature, which selects lava fields in a mild climate.

basaltic_volcanic.definition_note: Lunar lava tubes 'formed during the eruption of basaltic lava flows', and the Marius Hills Pit lies on mare (basalt) terrain (LROC Lunar Pit Atlas). Earth's match is ground dominated by basaltic volcanic rock (GLiM). Weighted x2: rock type defines a lava-tube site.

targets.name: Jezero Crater, Mars
targets.source_label: ESA topographic map of Jezero crater and surrounds (HRSC / MOLA)
targets.summary: Perseverance rover landing site: a Noachian lake basin with two fluvial deltas on the western edge of the Isidis impact structure, roughly 2.6 km below the Mars areoid.

precipitation.definition_note: Modern Mars has no stable liquid water at the surface and no liquid-water precipitation; only vapour and ice cycles operate. Scored against Earth's driest land.

vegetation.definition_note: No known biosphere: the surface is bare rock and regolith. The Earth equivalent is ground with no detectable vegetation (NDVI near 0).

annual_temperature_range.definition_note: Seasonal amplitude of daily-mean ground temperature at Jezero over Mars Year 36: daily means span 210 to 232 K. At 1.45 m the daily-mean amplitude is 16 K and the annual amplitude of daily-maximum air temperature reaches 35 K.

lst_diurnal_range.definition_note: Ground-skin temperature range on sol 189 (191 to 277 K), a high-insolation season; 56 K in low insolation. Beyond anything on Earth, so it is scored against Earth's largest day-night swing.

slope.definition_note: Measured: 3.4 deg RMS slope at a 50 m baseline on the smooth crater floor (7.09 deg for the full HiRISE study area, 11.29 deg on the rim; Kirk et al. 2021). A 50 m slope cannot be compared with a ~55 km regional slope, so the target is the terrain class 'gentle': Earth's 40th-percentile regional slope.

roughness.definition_note: PROXY: no Jezero-specific roughness is published. The modal MOLA RMS roughness of the northern lowlands (which include Isidis Planitia) is ~1 m. These plains are among the smoothest terrains on Mars, so the target is the terrain class 'smooth': Earth's 30th-percentile roughness.

elevation.definition_note: Jezero crater floor, about 2600 m below the Mars areoid. Not comparable with Earth's sea-level datum; weighted 0 by default.

mean_annual_temperature.definition_note: Not used for this target: the site is sunlit or seasonally lit, so absolute temperature is not the engineering challenge being matched.

basaltic_volcanic.definition_note: Not used: rock type is not part of this site's signature. Only the lava-tube habitat target scores basaltic rock.

targets.name: Gale Crater and Mount Sharp, Mars
targets.source_label: Gale crater (Curiosity rover site): layered central mound, Mount Sharp
targets.summary: Curiosity rover site: a crater floor rising into Mount Sharp, a layered sedimentary mound recording a change from clays to sulfates. Matched here on climate and terrain; mineralogy is not yet a criterion.

precipitation.definition_note: Modern Mars has no stable liquid water at the surface and no liquid-water precipitation; only vapour and ice cycles operate. Scored against Earth's driest land.

vegetation.definition_note: No known biosphere: the surface is bare rock and regolith. The Earth equivalent is ground with no detectable vegetation (NDVI near 0).

annual_temperature_range.definition_note: From the Gale Crater climate table (Curiosity REMS, Centro de Astrobiologia, 2012-2015, seasons normalised to Earth months): monthly means taken as (mean daily high + mean daily low) / 2 range from -55.5 C to -33.5 C. Air temperature, not ground temperature.

lst_diurnal_range.baseline: annual mean daily high minus low
lst_diurnal_range.definition_note: Mean daily high -5.7 C minus mean daily low -78.5 C (Curiosity REMS, 2012-2015). Air temperature; beyond anything on Earth, so it is matched to Earth's largest day-night swing.

slope.definition_note: Curiosity drives from the crater floor up the foothills of Mount Sharp, a mound several kilometres high: terrain class 'hilly', Earth's 75th-percentile regional slope. Editorial class; replace with a HiRISE DTM value.

roughness.definition_note: Layered mound foothills: terrain class 'hilly', Earth's 75th-percentile roughness. Editorial class.

elevation.definition_note: Not used: Mars heights are measured from the areoid.

mean_annual_temperature.definition_note: Not used for this target: the site is sunlit or seasonally lit, so absolute temperature is not the engineering challenge being matched.

basaltic_volcanic.definition_note: Not used: rock type is not part of this site's signature. Only the lava-tube habitat target scores basaltic rock.

targets.name: Utopia Planitia ice-rich ground, Mars
targets.source_label: NASA JPL (22 Nov 2016): MRO SHARAD radar finds buried ice in Utopia Planitia, as much water as Lake Superior
targets.summary: A vast northern plain where radar found buried, ice-rich ground: a candidate source of water for In-Situ Resource Utilization. Mars is colder than any ice-free ground on Earth, so the match is Earth's cold, barren, dry permafrost regime.
targets.location_note: Centre of Utopia Planitia (46.7°N, 117.5°E). Ice-rich deposits and pingo-like features lie at about 35-50°N, 80-115°E (Wikipedia, Utopia Planitia).

precipitation.definition_note: Modern Mars has no stable liquid water at the surface and no liquid-water precipitation; only vapour and ice cycle through the atmosphere.

vegetation.definition_note: No known biosphere: the surface is bare rock and regolith. The Earth equivalent is ground with no detectable vegetation (NDVI near 0).

annual_temperature_range.definition_note: Not used: no verified seasonal temperature range for Utopia Planitia.

lst_diurnal_range.baseline: Viking 1 lander site, air temperature 184 to 242 K
lst_diurnal_range.definition_note: NASA's Mars fact sheet gives a diurnal range of 184 K to 242 K (-89 to -31 °C) at the Viking 1 lander site. Beyond anything on Earth, so it is matched to Earth's largest swing. Air temperature at another site, used as Mars's typical swing.

slope.definition_note: Utopia Planitia is a large plain. Estimated class: Earth's 15th-percentile regional slope. No slope was measured at a comparable scale.

roughness.definition_note: A smooth plain with scalloped, ice-related hollows. Estimated class: Earth's 20th-percentile roughness.

elevation.definition_note: Not used: Martian heights are measured from Mars's own datum.

mean_annual_temperature.definition_note: Mars averages about -59 °C, colder than any ice-free ground on Earth. Clamping to Earth's coldest land would select the East Antarctic plateau. The target is Earth's 20th percentile instead (about -24 °C), inside the continuous-permafrost regime (mean surface temperature below -5 °C, Wikipedia: Permafrost). The model has no ice-cover layer, so coastal Antarctic ice can still match; ice-free permafrost needs that layer. Estimated class. Weighted x2: cold ground is what keeps the ice.

basaltic_volcanic.definition_note: Not used: rock type is not part of this site's signature. Only the lava-tube habitat target scores basaltic rock.
